extracted.intended_audience: attorneys, appellants, and parties involved in USPTO disciplinary appeals and requests for reconsideration before the USPTO Director (OED matters)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural criteria for filing and obtaining reconsideration or modification of a USPTO Director's final order under 37 C.F.R. § 11.56(c), as applied in disciplinary proceedings before the Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and single-request rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Following a final decision of the USPTO, either party may make a single request for reconsideration or modification of the decision if such request is filed within twenty days from the date of entry of the decision. See 37 C.F.R. § 11.56(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only one request is permitted and it must be filed within the 20-day window from entry of the Director's decision; failure to meet timeliness/single-request constraints bars reconsideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible bases for reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: No request for reconsideration or modification shall be granted unless the request is based on newly discovered evidence or error of law or fact, and the requestor must demonstrate that any newly discovered evidence could not have been discovered any earlier by due diligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must expressly rely on one of these bases. Broad assertions that the Director 'erred' without identifying a specific legal or factual error, or without new evidence that could not have been found earlier, are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrow and limited standard of review (analogue to FRCP 59/60)
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard of review used for § 11.56(c) is narrow and limited to circumstances involving new evidence, or to correct errors of law or fact; courts have looked to Rules 59(e) and 60 of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure for guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should frame motions with the tight standards of Rules 59(e)/60 in mind. Reconsideration is not a vehicle to raise new legal theories or reargue the record under a relaxed standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: New evidence must not have been available earlier
rubrics_metrics.description: Any new evidence submitted must not have been available before the issuance of the final decision; evidence available to a party prior to entry of judgment is not a basis for granting reconsideration as a matter of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To prevail on a newly discovered evidence theory, demonstrate (1) the evidence is genuinely new, (2) due diligence could not have discovered it earlier, and (3) the evidence is material to the issues decided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not a vehicle to relitigate or register mere disagreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for reconsideration should not be used to rehash arguments previously presented, to relitigate old matters, or to state a party's disagreement with a final judgment; 'mere disagreement does not support' reconsideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid submitting previously rejected arguments framed as 'errors'; instead focus on showing a distinct qualifying ground (new evidence or a true legal/factual error not previously presented).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extraordinary remedy — granted sparingly
rubrics_metrics.description: Reconsideration motions are extraordinary remedies reserved only for extraordinary circumstances and are seldom granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect a high bar; cite instances of 'extraordinary circumstances' only where record and law clearly support relief. Motions should concisely show why the case is an exception to the general rule of finality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances warranting reconsideration (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reconsideration may be appropriate where, for example, 'the Court has patently misunderstood a party, or has made a decision outside the adversarial issues presented to the Court by the parties, or has made an error not of reasoning but of apprehension.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If alleging such a circumstance, identify precise misapprehension or decision outside the issues (with record citations) rather than general dissatisfaction; this is one of the narrow categories that can support relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deference to trial judge/ALJ on credibility findings
rubrics_metrics.description: When findings are based on determinations regarding the credibility of witnesses, deference to the trial judge is required because only the trial judge can observe demeanor and tone of voice; credibility-based findings that are not internally inconsistent can 'virtually never be clear error.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenges to credibility determinations are rarely successful on reconsideration; to overcome deference, show internal inconsistency, record contradictions, or a clear procedural/legal error in evaluating testimony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of arguments not previously raised
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments not raised or developed during the hearing or on appeal are waived on reconsideration; first-time arguments in a reconsideration request are ordinarily deemed waived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all significant legal and factual claims are raised and developed at earlier stages (hearing and appeal) or they will be considered waived. If raising an argument on reconsideration, explain why it was not previously raised and why waiver should not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to develop legal arguments (no perfunctory mentions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments that are not appropriately developed in a party's briefing may be deemed waived; fleeting or single-paragraph mentions without citation or analysis do not preserve a challenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support legal challenges with specific citations, analysis, and record references; mere declarative disagreement with a sanction or ruling is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary/discovery complaints must be specific and timely
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that testimony or exhibits should have been stricken because documents were not provided are inadequate if the complaining party neither requested the documents in discovery nor identifies the specific missing documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When asserting discovery-based error, specify which document(s) were not produced, show that they were material, and explain why they could not have been obtained earlier despite due diligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction challenges require developed argumentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Challenges to sanctions (e.g., exclusion from practice) that are mere statements of disagreement and not supported by developed legal analysis or case law are waived and insufficient for reconsideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To challenge a sanction successfully, present a developed legal argument with relevant authority and explain why the sanction is disproportionate or legally erroneous under the record and precedent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relief and appellate rights following denial
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellant denied reconsideration is entitled to seek judicial review on the record in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia under 35 U.S.C. § 32 within thirty (30) days after the date of the order recording the Director's action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reconsideration is denied, timely pursue judicial review and comply with the 30-day filing requirement and applicable local rules (e.g., E.D. Va. Local Civil Rule 83.5).
